official_outline_path: Normal age-related findings and care of the well patient
Developmental stages: cognitive (eg, changes associated with normal aging)
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Normal cognitive aging in an independent older adult, emphasizing retrieval speed versus preserved semantic knowledge and learning capacity.

item.vignette: A 74-year-old retired teacher comes for a routine health visit. She lives alone, manages her finances and medications, drives without difficulty, and volunteers at a library twice weekly. During the past 2 years, she has noticed that she sometimes needs more time to recall the names of acquaintances, although the names usually come to her later. Her family has not noticed repetitive questioning, getting lost, or changes in judgment. Neurologic examination is normal.
item.lead_in: Compared with a healthy 25-year-old adult, which of the following patterns on cognitive testing is most consistent with normal aging in this patient?

options.A: Slower retrieval of names with preserved or greater vocabulary knowledge
options.B: Faster retrieval of names with reduced vocabulary knowledge
options.C: Slower retrieval of names with inability to form new memories
options.D: Unchanged retrieval speed with loss of knowledge of common word meanings
options.E: Faster retrieval of names with improved ability to multitask

item.tested_construct: Normal age-related cognitive change: slowed lexical/name retrieval with preserved semantic knowledge and retained capacity for new learning.

explanation.key_explanation: The history shows preserved independent function and only mild slowing of name retrieval, which is compatible with normal cognitive aging. Healthy older adults may take longer to find words or recall names, while semantic knowledge such as vocabulary is generally preserved and may be greater than in younger adults. They also retain the ability to learn new skills and form new memories.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Normal aging can slow word/name retrieval while preserving semantic knowledge and the capacity for new learning.
distractor_explanations.B: Normal aging is not characterized by faster lexical retrieval, and vocabulary knowledge is generally preserved rather than reduced.
distractor_explanations.C: Slower retrieval can occur with aging, but inability to form new memories is not an expected normal age-related change.
distractor_explanations.D: Loss of semantic knowledge for common word meanings is not an expected feature of normal aging; healthy older adults generally preserve vocabulary and language knowledge.
distractor_explanations.E: Normal aging does not typically improve multitasking, and older adults commonly show slower rather than faster word retrieval.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish normal cognitive aging from pathologic cognitive decline: normal aging may slow retrieval and some attentional processes without loss of independence, semantic knowledge, or the ability to form new memories.

evidence_map.claim: Healthy older adults may be slower to find words and recall names, while vocabulary and knowledge of word meanings are often preserved or greater.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Supports the key pattern of slower name retrieval with preserved semantic knowledge.

evidence_map.claim: Healthy older adults retain the ability to learn new skills and form new memories.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Makes inability to form new memories inconsistent with normal aging.

evidence_map.claim: Normal aging may include problems with multitasking and mild decreases in attention rather than improved multitasking.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Makes improved multitasking inconsistent with normal aging.

evidence_map.claim: Age-related cognitive changes commonly include slower recall, not faster recall; vocabulary is generally preserved.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Both components of option B run counter to expected normal-aging patterns.

evidence_map.claim: Normal age-related forgetfulness does not imply loss of language knowledge or functional independence; serious language/functional problems suggest a disorder beyond normal aging.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Loss of common word meanings is not a normal-aging pattern.

semantic_fingerprint.tested_construct: Normal cognitive aging: retrieval-speed slowing with preserved semantic knowledge
semantic_fingerprint.mechanism: Age-associated changes in cognitive processing and retrieval without pathologic loss of stored semantic knowledge or functional independence
semantic_fingerprint.lead_in_task: Choose the cognitive-test pattern most consistent with normal aging
semantic_fingerprint.correct_answer_concept: Slower name retrieval with preserved or greater vocabulary knowledge
reasoning_chain: Recognize preserved function and mild retrieval slowing
Classify as normal aging rather than neurocognitive disorder
Select preserved semantic knowledge with slower retrieval
distractor_misconceptions: equating retrieval slowing with inability to encode memories
